hero.heading: You don’t need to have the words yet.
hero.lead: Finding the words is what the room is for. Quiet Practice offers individual therapy, couples counselling, and counselling for teenagers — and a two-minute check to help you find the right place to start.

facts: In person on NE Alberta Street

servicesSection.title: The services
servicesSection.lead: Each page below says who it is for, how sessions work, and what the first one is actually like — in plain words, so you can decide from your own sofa.

items.title: Say hello
items.body: Call or email in whatever words you have. “I think I need to talk to someone” is plenty.

items.title: A free fifteen-minute call
items.body: We talk about what is going on and whether I am the right fit. If I am not, I will say so and suggest someone who is.

items.title: Your first session
items.body: Unhurried, confidential, and yours. By the third session we will have a shared plan that you have agreed to.

items.question: Do you take insurance?
items.answer: I am an out-of-network provider. You pay per session and I give you a monthly superbill to send to your insurer — many PPO plans reimburse 50 to 80 percent of the fee. I also hold a few reduced-fee places for people paying entirely out of pocket. Asking about money is a normal part of a first call.

items.question: How long will therapy take?
items.answer: Honestly: it depends, and you will never be strung along. We review how it is going together every six weeks or so. Some people come for twelve sessions around one clear thing; some stay a year because the work keeps earning its place. You can stop whenever you want, and a good last session is worth having.

items.question: Is what we talk about confidential?
items.answer: Yes, with the standard legal limits: risk of serious harm to yourself or someone else, abuse of a child or vulnerable adult, or a court order. For teenagers, we agree at the very start what stays private and what I will always share with parents — safety concerns, always; diary-level detail, never.

items.question: What if the check points me to the wrong service?
items.answer: Then nothing is lost. The check is a signpost, not a verdict — the free intro call is where we confirm fit, and people move between individual, couples, and teen work all the time. Start anywhere; starting is the hard part.

contact.title: The door is easy to knock on
contact.body: There is no intake portal and no phone tree — you reach me directly. Get in touch in whichever way feels lighter today, and we will take it from there.

crisisNote: If you or your teen need urgent help right now, a website is the wrong tool: call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US) or your local emergency number.
